To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large internal loop in a hairpin is required for a viral RNA to replicate and accumulate to high levels in plants.

a large symmetrical loop in the 3'-proximal hairpin of satC is necessary for robust accumulation of satC RNA in plants, and that this loop might be involved in additional processes in addition to repressing replication.
(1) The large symmetrical internal hairpin loop of a satellite RNA is required for efficient accumulation in plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of sequence requirements of a large internal loop of an H5 hairpin in a satellite RNA that functions in the negative control of replication.
the role of a viral RNA element in the regulation of viral RNA synthesis and the identification of sequence requirements for this function.
the identification of the structural and sequence requirements of a repressor element in a satellite RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LSL of satC is required for efficient replication and accumulation in both plants and protoplast systems.
sequence elements in both sides of the H5 LSL are necessary but not sufficient for robust satC replication in protoplasts and in plants.
the LSL is required for efficient satC replication in plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LSL is a complex RNA structure with a number of functions that include: (i) a cis-acting sequence element required for minus-strand synthesis; (ii) a cis- and trans-acting element required for plus-strand synthesis; and (iii) a trans-acting element that may be involved in RNA replication.
a large, symmetrical internal loop is required for efficient replication of a satellite RNA in plants.
the LSL is a complex structure that plays an important role in regulating satC replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LSL of H5 is not just a sequence that is conserved in the genus but is also a sequence with a functional significance in the virus.
the LSL is an RNA structural element that can be used to regulate viral RNA accumulation in plants.
the 14 base LSL of the 3’ proximal hairpin of the Carmoviruses is important for viral replication and accumulation in plants.
